title: Continuous coordinate partials give a continuous real differential
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $m\geq1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbf R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbf C$. Suppose that for every $1\leq j\leq m$ the real one-variable derivative $\partial_j f(x)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}f(x+te_j)\right|_{t=0}$ exists for every $x\in U$, and that each function $\partial_j f:U\to\mathbf C$ is continuous. Here $e_j$ is the $j$-th standard coordinate vector. Then $f$ is continuous and real Frechet differentiable on $U$, with $$Df(x)[h]=\sum_{j=1}^m h_j\partial_j f(x)\qquad(x\in U,\ h\in\mathbf R^m).$$ The map $x\mapsto Df(x)$ is continuous for the operator norm on real-linear maps $\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf C$.

source.place: WANTED: third edition, Theorem 9.21, continuous partial derivatives imply differentiability. Agent-formulated complex-valued version; this book is not present locally and has not been read.

proof.text: Fix $x\in U$ and write $a_j=\partial_jf(x)$ and $A_xh=\sum_j h_ja_j$. This is real-linear and $|A_xh|\leq(\sum_j|a_j|)\|h\|$, since $|h_j|\leq\|h\|$ for the Euclidean norm; thus it is continuous. Given $\varepsilon>0$, openness of $U$ and continuity of the finitely many partials at $x$ give $\delta>0$ such that $B(x,\delta)\subseteq U$ and $|\partial_jf(z)-a_j|\leq\varepsilon/m$ for every $z$ in that ball and every $j$. For $\|h\|<\delta$ put $p_0=x$, $p_j=x+\sum_{k\leq j}h_ke_k$. Every point $p_{j-1}+t h_je_j$, $0\leq t\leq1$, lies in this ball: its squared distance from $x$ is $\sum_{k<j}h_k^2+t^2h_j^2\leq\|h\|^2$.

source.place: norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment_01', lines 346–349; real scalar field and complex target.

proof.text: For each $j$ define $q_j(t)=f(p_{j-1}+t h_je_j)-t h_ja_j$ on the open preimage of $U$ under this affine line, which contains $[0,1]$. Its real derivative is $$q_j^{\prime}(t)=h_j(\partial_jf(p_{j-1}+t h_je_j)-a_j).$$ This uses only the one-variable partial derivative from the hypothesis: for $h_j\ne0$, substitute $s=h_ju$ in its defining difference quotient at $p_{j-1}+t h_je_j$, and subtract the derivative $h_ja_j$; for $h_j=0$, $q_j$ is constant. Extend $q_j$ and this derivative arbitrarily away from their open domain. At each point of $[0,1]$ the relative derivative is therefore unchanged, including both endpoints. The derivative bound from step 1 is $|q_j^{\prime}(t)|\leq |h_j|\varepsilon/m$. Apply the unit-interval derivative-bound lemma with $C=|h_j|\varepsilon/m\geq0$ to obtain $$|f(p_j)-f(p_{j-1})-h_ja_j|\leq |h_j|\varepsilon/m.$$ No continuity of $f$ in several variables has been assumed.

source.place: norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le_segment_01', lines 346–349; real scalar field and complex target.

proof.text: Sum the increments, using $p_m=x+h$ and cancellation of consecutive values of $f$. The triangle inequality gives $$|f(x+h)-f(x)-A_xh|\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{m}\sum_j|h_j|\leq\varepsilon\|h\|.$$ For every $\varepsilon>0$ this holds for all sufficiently small $h$, so the remainder divided by $\|h\|$ tends to zero as $h\to0$, $h\ne0$. This is exactly real Frechet differentiability at $x$ with differential $A_x$. It also proves continuity at $x$: use the same estimate with $\varepsilon=1$ to bound $|f(x+h)-f(x)|$ by $(1+\sum_j|a_j|)\|h\|$. Since $x$ was arbitrary the conclusions hold on $U$.

proof.text: For $x,y\in U$ and $\|h\|\leq1$, the differential formula gives $$|(A_y-A_x)h|\leq\sum_j|h_j|\,|\partial_jf(y)-\partial_jf(x)|\leq\sum_j|\partial_jf(y)-\partial_jf(x)|.$$ Taking the supremum over the unit ball yields the same bound for $\|A_y-A_x\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. At each fixed $x$ the right side tends to zero as $y\to x$ in $U$, being a finite sum of continuous functions vanishing at $x$. Thus $x\mapsto Df(x)=A_x$ is continuous in operator norm.
